    #50244. Re-grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade: Why the Heat and Bucks both look much worse now

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2348 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Re-grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade: Why the Heat and Bucks both look much worse now

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2348 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo will face the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time as an opponent on Wednesday, but it's a game that feels as though it's a half-decade or more in the making.
    • Industry observers note that the Bucks kept kicking the can down the road.
    • It has been revealed that now, Antetokounmpo plays for the Heat while the Bucks are in no man's land.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Giannis Antetokounmpo will face the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time as an opponent on Wednesday, but it's a game that feels as though it's a half-decade or more in the making. The Miami Heat were a rumored suitor for Antetokounmpo, who played his first 13 NBA seasons in Milwaukee, as far back as the buildup to his possible 2021 free agency, which the Bucks averted by trading for Jrue Holiday and ultimately winning a championship.

    Industry observers note that the Bucks kept kicking the can down the road. They secured another extension with Antetokounmpo in 2023 by trading for Damian Lillard. They stuck their fingers in their ears and pretended everything was fine when Lillard tore his Achilles in 2025, in the process bypassing the chance to trade Antetokounmpo with multiple years left on his contract when they could have maximized his trade value. In the end, though, Heat president Pat Riley did what he has done so many times before: he got his man.

    It has been revealed that now, Antetokounmpo plays for the Heat while the Bucks are in no man's land. We have around four weeks of data on how these teams are going to look after one of the bigger blockbusters in recent NBA history, so with their first head-to-head bout at hand, let's regrade the trade based on everything we now know.

    According to recent reports, let's start with the obvious positive: despite age- and injury-related fears, Antetokounmpo is still mostly himself. He is, by both the counting stats and the all-in-ones, playing either at the level of his Milwaukee peak or somewhere relatively close. He has at the very least been a top 10 player in the NBA this season, and you could argue him into the top five. Miami paid an All-NBA price and has gotten an All-NBA player.

    In a recent development, there are slight signs of slipping in his age-32 season that merit some examination, though they don't come close to triggering any real alarms. His free-throw rate is lower than it's been since 2018, for instance, but it's still near the top of the league. He's scoring 1.38 points per possession when shooting at the rim -- a very good figure that rates him in the 82nd percentile league-wide, per Synergy Sports. We just judge Antetokounmpo on a curve because he was in the 95th percentile last season and generally hovered around the mid-90s when he was winning MVPs and his 2021 championship.

    It has been revealed that this is, again, not a significant concern. He's still great, and he's supplementing his rim finishing with significant improvement from mid-range. After shooting below 39% from mid-range over the past five seasons combined, he's above 51% so far this season. We can say pretty safely at this point that the 3-point shot is never coming for Antetokounmpo, so this shot will be his pathway to both aging gracefully and combating the walls he'll see at the rim in the playoffs. If this is sustainable, it extends his prime another year or two and makes him close to unguardable while he remains near his physical peak. Thus far, last year's calf injuries have not recurred.

    Industry observers note that he's slipped defensively. That's almost undeniable. He contested around nine shots per game when he won Defensive Player of the Year in 2020. He's down to around six this season, and opponents are shooting 6% worse within six feet of the basket against Antetokounmpo than they are otherwise, per NBA.com tracking data. That figure was 20.4% in 2020. The all-in-ones share this basic opinion: still good, no longer great. The tape shows an older player who paces himself defensively. He can still summon greatness for stretches, but he's not in the All-Defense mix seriously anymore.

    That brings us to the bigger picture. When you trade as much as Miami did, the question is never just whether the player is good enough to justify the cost, but whether the team is. Heat fans would point to the team's ongoing 8-2 stretch following its 0-4 start to suggest that it was. Count me as a remaining skeptic.

    According to recent reports, most of those victories came against either the bottom of the league -- the Kings, the Jazz, they needed overtime to beat the Clippers! -- or injured opponents. No Tyrese Haliburton in the Pacers win. No Jalen Duren against the Pistons. No Evan Mobley against the Cavaliers. No Amen Thompson against the Rockets, playing the second night of a back-to-back. They've faced only two true heavy hitters at full strength, the Lakers and Timberwolves, and they stood no chance against either.

    Industry observers note that the theory of this team relies on a top-five defense. The offense is simply too reliant on shot creation out of its bigs -- Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo -- to be the leading unit for a champion. The early defensive returns have thus far been discouraging, though in fairness, no team has been unluckier on wide-open opponents' 3s. Even during the 8-2 stretch, they're allowing 48.4 points in the paint per game, a well-below-average figure. Their transition defense is nothing special and they're so-so rebounders. They've hung their hat on turnover-generation, but they're by no means elite on that front. The raw numbers are bad. The truth is closer to fine when you factor in luck. They haven't been great, which is what they need to be.

    According to recent reports, part of the problem is that they need to play defensively deficient players -- most notably Klay Thompson and, if he eventually re-earns his rotation spot, Tim Hardaway Jr. -- in order to survive offensively. You can get away with that if everyone else is great. Antetokounmpo has taken a step back. Andrew Wiggins has been a mess. Erik Spoelstra is a defensive miracle worker, but the players here just haven't lived up to expectations. Davion Mitchell has become so notable offensively that even he's slipped a bit on that end.

    Recent findings suggest that mitchell's playmaking has been a godsend, and a pretty surprising one in context. The Heat tried and failed to get the Bucks to take Mitchell instead of Kasparas Jakučionis in the trade. There's no telling how bad things would be without Mitchell at this stage, but we're still talking about a pretty limited scorer who nearly doubled his 3-point volume and free throw attempt rate in a single season. Miami probably can't expect him to carry this sort of burden forever. Pelle Larsson is more of a connector than a creator in his own right. Down the line, another guard who can create off of the dribble is probably needed here, especially without a strong Antetokounmpo-Adebayo two-man game forming thus far.

    According to recent reports, the paths to improvement here are narrow here. The Heat are pressed up against a first-apron hard cap, and they'd need Charlotte's cooperation to amend the protection on their 2027 selection if they wanted to trade even a single first-round pick at this deadline. It's going to take a little while to meaningfully upgrade the supporting talent here, and the rest of the Heat offseason reflected that.

    According to recent reports, they could have perhaps generated the cap flexibility to retain Norman Powell. They elected instead to let him walk, and when they extended Wiggins, they chose to front-load the deal by using his player option rather than spreading the money out to create more immediate hard cap room. Rather than signing a mid-level free agent to a multi-year deal, they added the older Hardaway on just a one-year contract, presumably to maintain optionality going into next summer.

    If Antetokounmpo were 28, this patience might make sense. He turns 32 in less than a month. The time to go all-in around him is now. It's an ironic middle ground that the Heat have put themselves in. Miami could justify the cost it paid for Antetokounmpo only through immediate contention, yet they're slow-playing the roster build in what you would expect, just based on the standard aging curve, to be the best individual season left in his career. It really doesn't make sense to do this halfway.

    We're talking about the Heat here. They've made the Finals with less talent than they have now, and they are organizationally opposed to intentional rebuilds. There was never a conversation here about, say, trading Adebayo and starting over as opposed to pushing chips in for someone like Antetokounmpo. But if a few years pass and the Heat don't at least make the conference finals with this core, it's going to be worth wondering if that's the path they should have taken. The early returns here are mixed. The Heat bet their future on a single player. He may be good enough to warrant that investment, but the jury's still out on whether their team actually is.

    In a recent development, the Bucks dug themselves an enormous hole by refusing to trade Antetokounmpo when the whole world knew they should have. It was over the moment Lillard tore his Achilles. At that point, Antetokounmpo had two years left on his contract, so hypothetical rental trades would have been feasible. He was younger and he hadn't yet lost a year to calf injuries, so his value was higher. Asset-rich teams like the Spurs and Rockets might have been interested. Had the Bucks moved Antetokounmpo in 2025, they would have gotten substantially more than they wound up getting. Instead, they made the disastrous decision not only to keep him but also to waive and stretch Lillard to sign Myles Turner. Yikes.

    In a recent development, when the Bucks finally realized they'd reached the point of no return, Antetokounmpo, as an expiring contract, had complete control of the situation. At least four teams with strong offers were turned away because Antetokounmpo simply wasn't interested in extending with them, according to ESPN. He only wanted the Heat or Celtics. Given those circumstances, the Bucks still managed the negotiations as well as they reasonably could have. They used the Celtics as an effective scare tactic to compel Miami to give up pretty much all of its available draft capital, plus Jakučionis instead of Mitchell.

    You can win a negotiation and still lose a trade, though, when most of the things the other team had to give in a trade just weren't that valuable. The massive swing piece here was Kel'El Ware, an extremely high-risk, high-reward young big man with star-level raw talent and a pretty iffy reputation when it comes to his motor and commitment. The Bucks, thus far, have gotten the worst version of him. He's playing less in his third season with the Bucks than he did in two years with the Heat despite being on the worst roster of his career. He's missing shots everywhere, his defense has been miserable, and if he's ever going to reach that sky-high ceiling, it's probably going to have to come on his third team.

    That, in a nutshell, is the problem here. The Bucks traded the greatest player in franchise history, one of the 25 or so best players the league has ever seen, and got no one who could credibly be considered a cornerstone moving forward. Ware looks like a swing and a miss. It's too early to say much on Nate Ament, but he's a No. 13 overall draft pick, so odds are, he's going to be fine and not much better. Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. are both about what they expected, but both will need to be paid next summer. Herro's presence exacerbates a preexisting glut of guards. His presence has forced last year's breakout guard, Ryan Rollins, to the bench. Maybe that makes him a bit cheaper as a free agent next summer. It also probably sours him on a future in Milwaukee.

    Speaking of the guard glut, the Gary Trent Jr. investigation looms large over this trade. The NBA set a notable precedent in the Kawhi Leonard case that it is willing to strip teams of draft picks acquired through trade. This is notable because the Bucks have so little control over their own first-round picks moving forward. The picks they got from the Heat in 2031 and 2033, at least for now, are the crown jewels of this trade. Both of them are theoretically vulnerable if the NBA finds that the Bucks circumvented the salary cap.

    Industry observers note that it's even worth wondering if the Bucks should or could have used the Antetokounmpo situation as an escape hatch on any preexisting agreements with Trent, if one actually existed. If the Bucks felt an obligation to pay Trent more than the market suggested he was worth, and if they knew they had so many guards that he was unlikely to factor into their rotation (he played less than 40 total minutes before bizarrely leading the Bucks in playing time in Sunday's loss to the Hawks despite coming off the bench), then why not use the leverage Antetokounmpo's availability granted them to foist Trent on Miami through a sign-and-trade? Of course, if the Bucks had the foresight to do this, they probably wouldn't be in this situation in the first place. For now, the investigation is ongoing and we know little beyond the sheer ridiculousness of the contract itself.

    The Bucks are 1-13 as of this writing. That, roughly, was to be expected. This was a bad team with Antetokounmpo, so inevitably, removing an MVP candidate was going to make it far worse. But to leave a trade involving a player of that caliber without a single blue-chip player or draft pick is frankly embarrassing.

    According to recent reports, the Bucks bungled this Antetokounmpo saga for a year, and even if they managed its end stages properly, they'd dug themselves so deep a hole that there was just no obvious way out of it. Now, it seems they may well have made the situation worse with Trent after the fact. This was an organization-wide debacle.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving.
    • As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    Recent findings suggest that the Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Recent findings suggest that rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    In a recent development, as things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    It has been revealed that alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    Though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the beauty of the NFL is its unpredictability. It's what keeps us coming back each Sunday, as we never quite know what's going to unfold. We might have a good idea, but more often than not, the consensus outcome fails to actually come to fruition. As difficult as it may be to try and predict what's around the corner in a given week, we've done a pretty good job this season of predicting the unpredictable.

    Recent findings suggest that for instance, last week we accurately put you on to both Zach Charbonnet and Josh Downs making waves that far surpassed their over/under gambling odds. We also told you to temper your expectations regarding Fernando Mendoza's first career start, which proved wise. Of course, we're not going to bat a thousand here given the nature of trying to see into the future, and we came up short in our predictions that Brock Purdy would ascend as the MVP favorite, along with Will Anderson Jr. falling two sacks shy of matching his single-game career high.

    This go-around, we turn our attention to a couple of individual performances, as well as highlight some developments in the playoff and award races that we wouldn't be shocked to see unfold in Week 11.

    All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Tony Pollard spent the first five seasons of his career in Dallas after the Cowboys selected him in the fourth round out of Memphis in 2019. The veteran back left the organization in 2024, inking a three-year, $21.75 million deal with the Titans. Now, for the first time since leaving the Cowboys, Pollard will face his former team on Sunday.

    The 29-year-old has a fantastic opportunity to get one over on his former team, which has struggled immensely to stop the run this season. In fact, the Cowboys are giving up 154.1 rushing yards per game on a 5.2 yards-per-carry clip this season, both the most in the NFL. Dallas is also giving up the third-most receiving yards to running backs and the most receiving touchdowns.

    This sets Pollard up for a dominant day out of Tennessee's backfield and continues what has been a white-hot stretch for him. Over his past three games, Pollard has rushed for 279 yards (5.1 yards per carry) and five touchdowns, while catching 14 of his 17 targets for 112 yards and another score.

    The way both Pollard and the Cowboys' run defense are trending, it wouldn't surprise us at all if he logs 150 scrimmage yards.

    In a recent development, gambling nuggets to note: Tony Pollard's O/U rushing yards prop for Week 11 is 65.5 (-110 to the Over). Meanwhile, Pollard's O/U rushing + receiving yards prop for Week 11 is 87.5 (-110 to the Over).

    According to recent reports, the Lions enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record, which is good for first place in the NFC North and slotted in as the No. 2 seed in the conference. Amid the team's five-game winning streak, however, Jared Goff has been a little loose with the football. The Lions quarterback has thrown four interceptions over his last three games, including two last week against the Patriots in Germany.

    Sources indicate that goff has thrown an interception in three straight games entering Sunday's contest with the Buccaneers, and it really should be four straight games. Before this streak started, Goff had two interceptions dropped by Packers defenders in Detroit's Week 7 matchup against Green Bay.

    Sources indicate that now, Goff faces a Tampa Bay defense that will not only be well rested after being on the bye in Week 10 but has a knack for snatching interceptions. The Buccaneers lead the league with 16 interceptions. Their 72.7 passer rating allowed is also second-best in the NFL and only looking up to the Vikings, so this has the potential to be a tough task for Goff to overcome. It also sets up a strong possibility that this pesky interception streak will continue.

    Gambling nugget to note: Jared Goff is +122 to throw at least one interception in Week 11.

    The Cleveland Browns get to kick their feet up and watch the action unfold across the league this weekend as they're at the moment on the bye. Before the break, the club vaulted into the AFC playoff picture and currently sits as the No. 7 seed with a 6-4 record. Even with Cleveland not playing this week, there's a strong opportunity for the franchise's playoff position to strengthen.

    Namely, they'll be rooting for the Eagles, who host the Steelers (at the moment the No. 6 seed). If Philadelphia pulls off the home upset over Pittsburgh (who hasn't won a road game against the Eagles since 1965), the Steelers would draw even with Cleveland with a 6-5 record. Because these teams split the season series, the next tiebreaker would be their record within the AFC North. The Browns (2-1) have a better division record than the Steelers (2-2) at the moment, so they'd leap ahead of them.

    On top of the Eagles, if the Panthers and/or Broncos pull off wins against the Ravens and Raiders, respectively, that'd further create some breathing room for Cleveland. By the time they emerge from their bye week and gear up for Week 12, I wouldn't be surprised if the Browns are the No. 6 seed.

    Gambling nugget to note: An Eagles, Panthers, Broncos moneyline parlay is +468.

    The Vikings have been the talk of the NFL for the bulk of the season thanks to their lethal defense, but they also got a massive boost right before the trade deadline by acquiring Kirk Cousins. The veteran quarterback provided immediate dividends in the club's Week 10 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, and will try to continue this storybook return to Minnesota when they take on the 49ers in Mexico City. The Vikings are a 3-point underdog in this matchup, but their defense certainly gives them a shot to pull off the upset.

    According to recent reports, not to mention that Brock Purdy is 0-2 against the Vikings in his career. In those games, Purdy's teams have averaged just 17 points per game, while he's thrown two touchdowns and committed four turnovers. If Minnesota forces Purdy to look like that once again, they are live to pull out the win.

    Sources indicate that provided they do, Minnesota suddenly has an opportunity to leap to the No. 1 seed in the NFC by the end of Sunday. Of course, that result is contingent on other factors playing out over the course of the slate, but it's not out of the realm of possibility. All the Vikings would need is for the Buccaneers to upset the Lions, dropping Detroit to 7-3 on the season. Then, if Minnesota beats the 49ers to move to 8-2, they leap up atop the division and, because of the newly acquired head-to-head tiebreaker, would jump over San Francisco as the top seed in the conference.

    Gambling nuggets to note: Vikings are +130 to beat the 49ers. The Buccaneers are +270 to beat the Lions. A Vikings and Buccaneers moneyline parlay is +751. Currently, the Vikings are +450 to finish the season as the No. 1 seed.

    The tightest award race in the NFL amongst players is Offensive Rookie of the Year. Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is the current favorite, and he's started just one game so far this season. While that speaks to the value of the quarterback position, it also highlights just how wide open the race is and how a player can burst onto the scene midseason and make a legitimate run.

    In that same vein, folks should start paying attention to Saints rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson.

    Sources indicate that the No. 8 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft had the first half of his rookie season erased due to a hamstring injury he suffered during the summer. However, Tyson returned to the field in Week 9 and has almost instantly started making an impact. Over two games, Tyson has been targeted 18 times and hauled in 15 catches for 110 yards. That includes an 11-catch, 80-yard showing last week against Carolina.

    Those receptions are tied for the most in the first two games of a career in Saints history. According to Pro Football Focus, Tyson joined Malik Nabers (2024) and Puka Nacua (2023) as the only receivers since 2020 to have at least 10 receptions in a game within their first two games played.

    With Latest Orleans' running game nonexistent and pass-heavy game scripts projected for the rest of the season, Tyson is set up nicely to put up some eye-popping numbers, especially if he's going to command about nine targets per game. That includes this week, when the Saints are 11.5-point underdogs to the Bears. That suggests they'll be playing from behind and will need to throw the football, which could continue to showcase Tyson.

    This might be the time to buy his Offensive Rookie of the Year stock.

    Gambling nugget to note: Jordyn Tyson is +1800 to win Offensive Rookie of the Year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 21.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • Recent findings suggest that rúben Amorim’s Manchester United faced Hürzeler’s Brighton on Matchday 22.
    • Manchester United started in a nominal 3-2-4-1 formation, which transitioned into a classic 3-2-5 shape in possession and a 5-4-1 shape out of possession.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 21.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League mit 0 Kommentaren.

    Recent findings suggest that rúben Amorim’s Manchester United faced Hürzeler’s Brighton on Matchday 22. While Manchester United focused on creating a pressing system that was as difficult as possible to bypass, Brighton once again showcased their incredibly challenging vertical play. You can find the tactical analysis of the match here.

    Manchester United started in a nominal 3-2-4-1 formation, which transitioned into a classic 3-2-5 shape in possession and a 5-4-1 shape out of possession. Amorim initially placed particular emphasis on a pressing system that varied in height.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, Brighton began in a nominal 4-4-2 formation. In possession, Hürzeler’s trademark positional rotations, vertical runs, and decoy movements for effective vertical play were continuously on display. Accordingly, Brighton operated flexibly from a variety of shapes, such as 4-2-4, 3-1-4-2, 2-3-2-3, and more. This flexibility makes Brighton’s possession game almost impossible to define through formations alone.

    Sources indicate that manchester United initially operated out of a 5-4-1 shape with varying defensive heights. This approach made it challenging for the opposition to play through, as different build-up phases required distinct patterns and connections. United’s central midfielders in the four-man line marked Brighton’s double pivot, Ayari and Baleba, man-to-man. The goal was to gain optimal control of Brighton’s central build-up play and apply immediate pressure whenever Brighton played through the middle.

    However, Brighton controlled the game during the first 10 minutes. Their holding midfielders positioned themselves close to the backline, creating a large gap between Manchester United’s five-man defensive line and the four-man midfield. This space was then exploited with various runs. When facing high pressing, left-back Estupiñán moved asymmetrically into the left half-space behind United’s first pressing block. This movement utilized the moment when Amad stepped out to press one of Brighton’s center-backs after bypassing Zirkzee.

    It has been revealed that united failed to adjust their pressing to this build-up variation throughout the match. As a result, this same pattern played a key role in Brighton’s build-up to the goal that made it 1-3.

    Against Manchester United’s mid-block, Brighton’s strikers, Welbeck and João Pedro, alternated their runs into the large space between the lines, targeting the gaps. This repeatedly allowed Brighton to bypass United’s first pressing line.

    Recent findings suggest that the 1-0 goal resulted from this setup, facilitated by a counter-movement. As striker Welbeck made a run into the space between the lines, he pulled his marker, De Ligt, a few steps out of the five-man backline. Simultaneously, winger Mitoma made a deep run into the space that opened up. De Ligt was caught in a dilemma between applying pressure and covering the depth. A long ball bypassed United’s entire pressing structure, leading to the goal.

    Another reason for Brighton’s dominance in the first 10 minutes lay in their defensive work. United built up in a very positionally structured 3-2-4-1(/-5) shape. Brighton countered with a 4-4-2 in their high press and a 5-4-1 in their mid-block. With Minteh marking Diogo Dalot man-to-man on the flank, the two different defensive shapes emerged depending on Dalot’s positioning. Brighton’s two strikers also pressed United’s center-backs, Maguire and Yoro, on that side, applying intense pressure on the ball carriers on United’s left.

    Sources indicate that on the other side, winger Mitoma positioned himself centrally when De Ligt had possession, cutting off the passing lane to Amad, who was positioned in the half-space. If the ball was played to full-back Mazraoui, Mitoma shifted out from the center to press, creating a cover shadow into the center. This approach effectively prevented United from creating any significant attacking threat on that flank as well.

    Around the 10th minute, the game shifted, and Brighton’s dominance began to fade. This was due to several adjustments made by United. To reduce the pressure on the ball carrier on the left side, the highly press-resistant Bruno Fernandes started to drop deeper, while the full-backs pushed higher. The resulting 3-3-4 shape was difficult for Brighton to press, as full-back Veltman, or the half-space defender in the five-man backline, was pulled out, and the space in behind could be exploited by either full-back Dalot or striker Zirkzee. This led to more possession phases for United and fewer pressing phases from Brighton.

    According to recent reports, another adjustment United made came from their 5-4-1 mid-block. The half-space defenders, De Ligt and Yoro, became much more aggressive in stepping out from the five-man backline to defend against the strikers making runs into the large space between the lines. This prevented Brighton’s strikers from turning after bypassing the first pressing block. To defend long balls to Mitoma, Mazraoui prioritized covering the space behind the advancing De Ligt. As a result, Brighton struggled to exploit the space between the lines and couldn’t progress as effectively into depth from their own possession.

    Sources indicate that additionally, Manchester United no longer pressed situationally from a 5-4-1 in a high press but instead switched to man-marking, with Zirkzee following the goalkeeper. This created much more pressure on the ball carriers for Brighton. Brighton also faced difficulties because the 5-4-1 system is much harder to break down than man-marking in a high press. This became evident in the sequence leading to the penalty goal. United suddenly switched to man-marking and forced the ball loss that preceded the penalty. United deservedly equalized.

    Recent findings suggest that after the 1-1, the game became more balanced. Brighton tried to break down the 5-4-1 mid-block, while United focused on their defensive game. When Manchester United switched to man-marking in the high press, Brighton continued to struggle and often lost possession. It is questionable why United didn’t press more boldly and high man-to-man during this phase to maintain better control of the game.

    From Brighton’s perspective, a situational, more extreme overload at the moment of transition into high pressing—such as in the central space just behind the first pressing block—could have been a possible solution to challenge United’s man-marking, putting them in a dilemma between applying pressure and defending 1v1 on the wings.

    In possession, Brighton’s players frequently adjusted their positioning with small movements, creating fresh passing lanes, changing passing angles, and occupying spaces that forced the opponent into pressing reactions. Below, I have outlined the main advantages of three of the most frequently used shapes by Brighton against United, as well as the necessary reactions from the opponent.

    Sources indicate that another factor that makes Brighton’s vertical play difficult to defend is the continuous variety of space-creating or counter-movement runs into depth. These consistently create dilemmas and positional problems for the defenders. Below, I have graphically illustrated some selected runs used against United:.

    Despite Brighton’s possession game, Manchester United was able to prevent significant goal-scoring opportunities initially. From their 5-4-1 structure, the center-backs repeatedly defended aggressively, stepping out. Additionally, after bypassing the four-man midfield, it would drop back into position. This “recovery defense” made it difficult for Brighton to develop effective build-up play and exploit opened spaces. Furthermore, United’s players were well-prepared for potential through balls. In particular, the full-backs consistently intercepted balls played behind the defensive line.

    Towards the end of the first half and into the second half, small (forced?) mistakes began to creep into United’s pressing. While the failure to step out with Ugarte in the man-marking high press in the 39th minute and the failure to step out with De Ligt in the space between the lines in the 38th minute went unpunished, the delayed step-out by Yoro led to Brighton’s deserved 1-2 at that point.

    Especially in the second half, Brighton adapted to the man-marking high press by having center-backs step inside, breaking free from the cover shadow, when pressing the goalkeeper. This allowed them to find the open player in build-up, and Brighton lost possession less frequently.

    Sources indicate that longer defensive phases in the mid-block for Manchester United followed. To break down this block, Brighton’s possession play became less positionally rigid. Much more frequently, certain zones were overloaded. In particular, the space between the lines and the half-spaces were repeatedly occupied by multiple players to create numerical superiority and apply pressure.

    United, on the other hand, struggled to create any significant goal-scoring chances. The high press could have been more effective with a brief orientation from the player pressing the goalkeeper to position the inward-dropping center-back into a cover shadow. From the 5-4-1 mid-block, too few dangerous ball recoveries and transition situations were created.

    Recent findings suggest that even from their own possession, Manchester United created too few goal-scoring opportunities. When Amorim’s team did get chances, it was typically through a ball played behind the wide players of the five-man backline. At the moment the press was triggered (when Brighton stepped out to the outer center-back), the forward half-space player dropped deep, and the winger made a run in behind. However, the lack of other ways to break the press led to too much predictability in United’s possession play.

    As a result, the second half became more one-sided, with Brighton repeatedly pressing and trying to put United’s press under pressure. This ultimately succeeded, leading to a deserved 3-1 victory for Hürzeler’s team.

    Recent findings suggest that amorim’s press, which was difficult to break down, was ultimately cracked by Hürzeler. It is questionable whether more frequent defensive pressing, alternating with situational man-marking high pressing, might have been a better approach against Brighton, in order to better tighten the space between the lines and the area behind the defense, making the game in depth more difficult. Despite a higher mid-block, Manchester United hardly created any dangerous transition situations. This is an area that needs improvement.

    According to recent reports, hürzeler’s team, on the other hand, once again played highly attractive possession football. Frequent positional rotations, shifts in formations, overloads, and space-creating runs make Brighton’s possession game very enjoyable to watch. For the opponent, these constant shifts in zones over an extended period are incredibly difficult to defend. It is very likely that we will see more teams adopting similar principles in possession in the future.

    Grading NFL quarterbacks on rookie contracts: Caleb Williams, C.J. Stroud kick careers into high gear

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There is nothing more valuable in the NFL than rostering a star quarterback on a rookie contract.
    • To make the most of the opportunity, though, that quarterback must be a legitimate standout.
    • It has been revealed that teams with slow-developing or underperforming young quarterbacks face the other side of this equation: the frustration of having enough cap space to field stars at other positions while lacking serviceable play at the most key position of all.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There is nothing more valuable in the NFL than rostering a star quarterback on a rookie contract. The financial flexibility that comes with a highly affordable signal-caller cannot be overstated. That's partly why the New England Patriots made a run to the Super Bowl last year and why the Chicago Bears are poised to do the same in 2026.

    To make the most of the opportunity, though, that quarterback must be a legitimate standout. Drake Maye was nearly the league MVP a year ago. Caleb Williams is in contention this season. They and a few others are in line for massive contract extensions when they become eligible.

    It has been revealed that teams with slow-developing or underperforming young quarterbacks face the other side of this equation: the frustration of having enough cap space to field stars at other positions while lacking serviceable play at the most key position of all. In many cases, this results in the quarterback's career flaming out and the team looking back to the draft for another swing at finding the face of the franchise. A couple of squads might see that play out in the months to come.

    Below are grades for all 12 starting quarterbacks who are on their rookie contracts.

    In just his second year as a pro, Maye achieved two feats that no other player on their rookie contract can boast. In fact, in reaching the Super Bowl and finishing one first-place vote shy of the MVP award, Maye stepped closer to glory than most quarterbacks in the league have at any point in their career regardless of contract status. Regression in his third season has come in the form of immense turnover issues (he's tied for second-most through 10 weeks with 13) and a .500 record, but some of that can be attributed to the Patriots roster being depleted by injuries. Speaking of which, Maye's season might be over because of the ankle injury he sustained in Munich in Week 10.

    In a recent development, the step backward in 2026 and the ankle issue cast uncertainty over what Maye's next contract will look like if he signs one when he becomes eligible for an extension this offseason. But there is no doubt that he is the locked-in quarterback of the present and future for the Patriots. His proven upside is greater than that of any other signal-caller on a rookie deal.

    The blame for the Houston Texans' underwhelming campaign cannot be directed at C.J. Stroud. While his inconsistency in 2024 and 2025 capped the team's success, his performance this year is the only thing keeping the Texans even remotely competitive in the postseason hunt. His return to the tremendous form that made him a standout rookie has been a pleasant development and puts him in line for a massive payday.

    When he won the Offensive Rookie of the Year award in 2023, Stroud led the NFL in passing yards per game and interception rate. His numbers this season in both of those categories (273.6 ypg, 0.9 INT%) are almost identical to the ones that put him at the top of the league.

    When the Texans inevitably sign Stroud to a lucrative extension, they will bet that the campaigns bookending his four-year career are more indicative of what is to come than the two in the middle.

    Sources indicate that through 26 games, it remains unclear whether Cam Ward is a viable long-term starter in this league. The Tennessee Titans will have a tough decision to make at the end of the year: draft another quarterback or add pieces around Ward when they make four selections in the first two rounds? The second-year surge they hoped would come from last year's No. 1 pick has not arrived, so their patience is about to be put to the test.

    Given that they are actively deconstructing the roster by trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker at the trade deadline, it is clear the Titans prioritize developing their young players over making desperation moves to make the roster competitive as right now constructed. That, along with their willingness to keep Tony Pollard and routinely add talent to the wide receiver group, suggests they want to give Ward every opportunity to improve. The next eight games will go a long way in determining whether Tennessee should stick to that plan or seek another option on draft day.

    It has been revealed that no team has been more prolific at winning one-possession games since 2025 than the Denver Broncos, and much of the credit goes to Bo Nix. He led the league in game-winning drives last year with seven and leads in both fourth-quarter comebacks (five) and game-winning drives (six) in 2026. Of course, it would be preferable if Nix helped put enough points on the board over the first three quarters that he did not need to pull off heroics in the final minutes, but at least he continues to deliver when his back is against the wall.

    This season is thus far the least productive of Nix's three-year career by completion rate, success rate, yards per game, and passer rating. Some of that regression might be attributable to the offensive coordinator change, which prompted Sean Payton to reclaim play-calling duties in Week 5. What is promising is that Nix's last three games were arguably his best of the campaign, so he might be rounding back into form just in time for the stretch run.

    Even with a slow start to the year, Nix has been everything the Broncos need since he joined them in 2024. And if not for his ankle injury last postseason, he might have played in the Super Bowl. There is no reason to think Denver will not invest in him when the time comes.

    It will take more time to accurately gauge Fernando Mendoza's outlook as an NFL starter. His debut, as should be expected, had its ups and downs. He took six sacks, completed a modest 17 of 29 passes, but scored his first touchdown on a 10-yard run to the end zone. In all, it was a milquetoast showing against a daunting Seattle Seahawks defense.

    In a recent development, the Las Vegas Raiders need to bolster their wide receiver group in the months to come in order to give Mendoza the requisite weapons to succeed. The tight end tandem of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer should help the No. 1 pick get his feet wet, though.

    Recent findings suggest that J.J. McCarthy might be saving his career in real-time. The inability to stay healthy and the lackluster play when he was on the field during his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings made him an undeniable bust -- so much so that the Vikings demoted him to the No. 3 line on their depth chart and moved on from him for pennies on the dollar when the New York Giants came calling for a trade earlier this year. With the change in scenery, however, has come marked improvement.

    McCarthy's Giants debut was astounding: A 243-yard fourth quarter. Since he earned the starting job, he has completed 66.3% of his passes for 224 yards per game with a touchdown and an interception. He went 2-1 in those starts. That is not half bad for someone who joined the team five weeks into the season. There are still obvious flaws in his game, but McCarthy has helped the Giants maintain their lead in the NFC East so far, and that is about all they could have asked for when they traded for him.

    Recent findings suggest that the best-case outcome for McCarthy the rest of the way is that he proves himself as a starting-caliber talent and latches on somewhere else in 2027. This is Jaxson Dart's team when he returns to full strength next year. Perhaps the most likely scenario is for McCarthy to settle in as his backup, continue to develop and cement himself as one of the NFL's best No. 2s. That would still be a disappointment considering he is a former No. 10 overall pick, but it would be a step forward from where he began the year.

    Elbow dislocations and a couple of minor lower-body injuries halted Jayden Daniels' momentum in the wake of a remarkable rookie season in which he won Offensive Rookie of the Year, finished seventh in MVP voting and took the Washington Commanders to the NFC Championship Game. He has been proficient when healthy since then, but he has only played 14 games since 2024, and the Commanders are just 4-9-1 even with him in the lineup over the last two seasons. His career thus far is a mixed bag, including the highest highs for a rookie quarterback and the lows of a middling team.

    It has been revealed that the elite rushing prowess that helped him lead the NFL in success rate as a rookie has regressed a bit, but he is a more accurate passer who this year paces the league in interception rate and who is on track to set a career high in yards per game. Again, there is give and take.

    According to recent reports, if the Commanders can upgrade their offensive line and increase their depth behind the injured Terry McLaurin at wide receiver, Daniels would finally have enough help around him to potentially take Washington back to its 2024 heights and solidify himself as a top-tier quarterback. He is not the problem in Washington.

    In a recent development, williams and the Bears are on a steep ascent to the top of the league. Individually, Williams is on a trajectory that may one day lead him to an MVP award. And from a team perspective, his climb into stardom is the catalyst behind the Bears' surge toward the front of the Super Bowl race.

    Industry observers note that the four-interception debacle in his last outing was an aberration in what has otherwise been a breakout season for the third-year quarterback. Prior to the setback, he showed an increased comfort in Ben Johnson's high-octane offense and took care of the ball about as well as anyone. Even after that showing, this is the best version of Williams the NFL has seen, with his career-best passer rating, uncanny sack avoidance, and 257.7 passing yards per game.

    It feels like this is the start of a superstar career.

    It has been revealed that from Weeks 1-5, Bryce Young emerged as a dark-horse MVP candidate. The second quarter of the season brought him back down to Earth. In totality, this is still by far the best year of his career, and it could not have come at a more crucial time as he approaches a pivotal offseason in which the Carolina Panthers must decide whether to pick up his fifth-year option, sign him to an extension or begin a separation process.

    It has been revealed that coach Dave Canales seems to have a deep understanding of Young's abilities and how best to use them. Young has done nothing but improve under his tutelage. His down weeks are still problematic, but when he is on, Young has been the best version of himself this year. Take his yardage numbers, for instance: the 266.3 yards per game the Heisman Trophy winner averages this season are far greater than the 188.2 of his previous career-best campaign.

    According to recent reports, young's development has been a slow burn, but it has been linear and remains on the right track. This is a quarterback Carolina can keep building around.

    It has been revealed that the New Orleans Saints' motto is to air it out, and they have a quarterback who can do that. Coach Kellen Moore put a lot on Tyler Shough's plate over his first 18 starts and, thus far in 2026, tasked him with throwing the third-most passes per game at 38.1. Across that hefty workload, Shough turned in a middle-of-the-pack passer rating, which is commendable for a quarterback in his sophomore professional season.

    If the Saints had a better defense, they would probably stand tall atop the NFL's worst division, and the conversation around Shough would be more positive. Instead, he is merely keeping New Orleans somewhat afloat in a division that could feature a sub-.500 champion. As he continues to build a connection with prized rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson and maintains a highly productive link with Chris Olave, it will become clearer whether he is a true franchise quarterback. But over two half-seasons as a starter, his early returns as a second-round pick are quite positive.

    The stop-and-start nature of Michael Penix Jr.'s three-year career makes it hard to judge fairly. He cannot be faulted for his torn ACL last year and the Atlanta Falcons' questionable management of the quarterback room the year prior. What is up for grading, though, is what Penix has done on the field, and over 20 starts, it is an average-to-slightly-below-average performance.

    With all of the star talent on the Falcons offense, the team needs its quarterback to perform at a high level and get the most out of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. As they enter the prime of their careers, it is paramount that Penix makes strides. The franchise cannot afford to let its two greatest assets go to waste. In that sense, Penix's slow development is a problem. But at the same time, his flashes suggest that there is a franchise quarterback in him. Back-to-back three-touchdown games in October were emblematic of the ceiling that made him worthy of a first-round pick.

    The arm strength Carson Beck lacked in his final year of college is back. The further removed he gets from his UCL injury at Georgia, the more he looks capable of playing in the NFL. But that does not mean he will thrive as the Arizona Cardinals' starter in the second half of the season, nor does it mean the team should not draft a quarterback with its 2027 first-round pick. Beck was dreadful in Week 10 in his debut, throwing a pair of interceptions, taking five sacks, and losing 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams. Then again, what third-round rookie would thrive in his first career start, with a depleted wide receiver group and against a top-10 defense?

    Arizona will do its due diligence in the coming weeks to see what it has in Beck. More likely than not, it does not have a franchise quarterback.

    Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He highlighted few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    Recent findings suggest that the Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the massive-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    In a recent development, coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by fresh owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    It has been revealed that the Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    It has been revealed that eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

    #50237. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
    • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
    • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    Industry observers note that it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward promptly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    In a recent development, devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    According to recent reports, you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

    Sources indicate that trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

    It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

    Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

    The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

    Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

    Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

    According to recent reports, decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 5.

    Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 3.

    Top right. Sudden death now effectively.

    Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

    Rolls it casually past the right post.

    Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

    Leeds United 2 Manchester United 3.

    Leeds United 2 Manchester United 2.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 2.

    Bottom right. Took it very promptly.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

    Smacks it even higher into the top right.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 0.

    So there will be another short delay.

    And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

    The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

    It has been revealed that not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

    Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

    Recent findings suggest that two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

    It’s like Euro 2016 all over again.

    Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

    Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

    Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

    It has been revealed that enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

    Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

    The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

    Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

    Industry observers note that there will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

    Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

    Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

    According to recent reports, clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

    In a recent development, jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

    Yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

    Understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

    Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

    Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

    Recent findings suggest that zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

    Recent findings suggest that couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

    According to recent reports, just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue.     Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

    While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

    Industry News: Between a Lack of Stability and Connection Issues
