    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    What Cowboys' Christian Parker said about demotion: DC considered leaving, pushed back on decision

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys put first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker in a no-win situation.
    • Recent findings suggest that cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer left Parker in a bizarre limbo state after stripping him of his defensive play-calling responsibilities and giving them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine for the rest of the season.
    • Sources indicate that teams regularly fire coordinators in-season, and they also let coordinators fight through adversity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys put first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker in a no-win situation.

    Recent findings suggest that cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer left Parker in a bizarre limbo state after stripping him of his defensive play-calling responsibilities and giving them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine for the rest of the season. Yet, Schottenheimer is keeping Parker on staff as the defensive coordinator to lead defensive meetings and build the defensive game proposal.

    Sources indicate that teams regularly fire coordinators in-season, and they also let coordinators fight through adversity. Dallas did a little bit of both with Parker, which is certainly unique. That's why, when addressing the move on Thursday, Parker called his situation "not ideal.".

    In a recent development, "Not an ideal situation for me personally, but it's what's best for the team at this current point," Parker said. "So that's how we're moving forward. Continuing to prepare and operate in the same way that we've been doing during the week to have the goal of winning on Sunday.".

    Sources indicate that some coaches in Parker's shoes would have walked out the door after being essentially neutered professionally. Parker noted he considered it as an option, yet he chose to stay.

    According to recent reports, "I think you can always choose to do that, right? Yeah, exactly," Parker noted. "[But] we didn't even get to the point of discussing that. I think initially it's going to stink, right? So initially in your mind, you're thinking about all the things and in my opinion, that would've been running from it.

    It has been revealed that "And at the end of the day, I got a job to do, and my job is to be the defensive coordinator of the Dallas Cowboys. Whether that is calling plays on Sunday, obviously that's not the case anymore, but on ... whatever day we play, there is a focus level that I need to have. There's a contribution that I still have to be able to maintain. That is regardless of feelings and anything else.".

    Parker, who at 34 is the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, made it clear that he lobbied hard with Schottenheimer to remain the DC with full responsibilities. But he said, "At the end of the day, that was a decision that was made.".

    Industry observers note that that decision came after another loss in Week 11 when Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in franchise history. In the aftermath of another frustrating defensive effort, the Cowboys now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).

    Recent findings suggest that parker confirmed everything Schottenheimer unveiled on Wednesday about his duties remaining the same during the week going forward, outside of play-calling responsibilities. What has also remained the same in Dallas over the years is the defense's inability to play sound football.

    According to recent reports, per CBS Sports Research, the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers.

    Schottenheimer saying Parker has a "very bright future here as our defensive coordinator" comes off as if he's talking about a first-round-pick quarterback he has to bench because the speed of the game is too fast. Schottenheimer disagreed that he is "benching" Parker, but Parker himself drew some parallels with his players in that regard.

    He pulled 2025 second-round pick edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku from the starting lineup in Week 6, and Parker mentioned it would be hypocritical for him to not have the same mature, steady attitude as a player when dealing with a similar demotion.

    According to recent reports, "Yesterday when I saw Eze, he's like, 'Hey, remember what you told me?'" Parker said. "Because I told him, 'Look, this is changing at the start of the game. This has not changed the second, third, fourth quarter. It doesn't change anything that we expect from you when you go out on that field.'.

    "So if I'm telling Eze that, how can I not tell myself that? And it's not about me, it's about this team.".

    The timing for Parker is unfortunate because Dallas' next two games provided him a chance to rebound against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles. However, Parker doesn't see his situation that way.

    According to recent reports, "There's never a right time for anything like this. So our focus is forward. It doesn't matter who we're playing.".

    Industry observers note that speaking of looking forward, Parker's future in Dallas is very unclear at the moment. Does he expect to return to the Cowboys as their defensive coordinator in 2027, like Schottenheimer said he believed he could?

    Frankfurt’s pressing adjustments secure victory over Galatasaray – MH

    📅 22 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1377 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.
    • Industry observers note that eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul.
    • According to recent reports, frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.

    Industry observers note that eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul. After about ten minutes, Frankfurt were trailing 0-1, but thanks in part to adjusted pressing, they were able to turn the game around. What follows is an aspect analysis of Frankfurt’s attacking press against the Istanbul side’s build-up play.

    According to recent reports, frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1. Ahead of the two midfielders Chaibi and Larsson, Uzun operated in the No. 10 role. On the left flank, winger Knauff played in front of left-back Brown. When dropping into a deeper defensive press, this structure shifted into a 4-4-2, with Burkardt and either Uzun or Knauff forming the first pressing line. In the transition to the attacking press, they shifted man-oriented as usual.

    Industry observers note that galatasaray also began in a nominal 4-2-3-1. In possession, their structure changed depending on the depth of their build-up, forming something like a 3-2-5 or 4-2-4 through the positioning of the full-backs. Width on the right side was provided by winger Sané, and on the left by full-back Elmalı. Left winger Akgün frequently moved inside, acting as a kind of “free player.” Meanwhile, right-back Sallai tucked in slightly in higher possession phases to help form a back three in the build-up.

    Galatasaray’s build-up was characterized by frequent rotations. Their basic reference point was the previously described 3-2-5. From this shape, they consistently sought positional interchanges in order to manipulate the opponent’s man-marking in the pressing phase. On the left side, Elmalı, who provided width, was able to vary his height. In deeper build-up phases, he often dropped further back, while he also regularly positioned himself on the last line. Winger Akgün was tasked with creating central overloads and repeatedly moved inside, at times even drifting over to the right side. In response to the full-back pushing high, the left holding midfielder, Lemina, rotated into the left-back position. Striker Yılmaz, in turn, shifted into the left half-space when the full-back stayed deeper and the winger dropped centrally.

    Galatasaray’s left-sided rotations force Frankfurt’s pressing players into constant reorientation.

    In a recent development, the purpose of these rotations was to manipulate man-marking and tie down specific Frankfurt players. Because winger Akgün frequently dropped into central areas, the two centre-backs, Koch and Theate, were occupied. Akgün positioned himself in front of striker Yılmaz in order to stretch the last line and create 1v1 opportunities. This produced a variety of different build-up structures, which required Frankfurt to constantly reorient themselves. For example, if Elmalı pushed high, he had to be tracked by Collins, and Galatasaray’s four attacking players tied down Frankfurt’s entire back line. This significantly complicated Frankfurt’s transition into man-marking, as the positioning of the forwards forced centre-back Theate to cover long distances during handovers.

    Since all players in the back line are occupied, defensive handovers become more difficult.

    Frankfurt’s plan, as in previous matches, was to shift into man-marking from a +1 overload through the handover of the opponents’ centre-backs and full-backs. The advantage of this approach is that spaces on and behind the last line can initially be secured, while the risk of a long ball leading to a 1v1 situation is minimized by having an additional covering player.

    According to recent reports, at the same time, after steering the opponent’s attack, the transition into man-marking could be executed to apply maximum pressure on the ball carrier. Depending on the opponent’s structure and build-up sequences, Frankfurt adapted their pressing schemes. For instance, they could vary the distance to their opponents during the pressing jump: larger distances allowed for greater security in coverage, while smaller distances created more immediate pressure.

    According to recent reports, galatasaray tried to make these handover moments as difficult as possible for Frankfurt by forcing the distances at the moment of transition into man-marking to become as large as possible. The aforementioned rotations, for example, forced Theate into long runs to pick up winger Sané, so that Brown could then jump out to the still unmarked and deeper-positioned right-back of Galatasaray.

    Industry observers note that because of Galatasaray’s attackers’ positioning, Theate and Brown are forced into long pressing runs. On top of that, Theate finds himself caught between two opponents due to the rotations.

    It has been revealed that galatasaray also tried to open up the center through certain rotations, aiming to draw Frankfurt’s midfielders out of central areas. Frankfurt tracked man-to-man with Larsson on half-space player Gündogan and Uzun on the deeper right-sided pivot Torreira. Depending on the side of build-up, Chaibi was prepared to jump onto the more advanced pivot, Lemina. Because Lemina often rotated into the full-back position, Doan frequently picked him up, leaving Chaibi or Collins (depending on the movements of Akgün and Elmalı) unexpectedly without a direct opponent. At the same time, Gündogan and Torreira sometimes rotated in opposite directions, which created difficulties for Frankfurt in terms of handovers in central areas.

    In a recent development, because Frankfurt found it increasingly difficult to press Galatasaray’s build-up through their usual handover approach, from around the 15th minute they opted for tighter marking distances to transition more promptly into full man-marking. Brown pushed up directly, Theate went straight onto Sané, while Collins and Koch marked the two remaining forwards. This created a 3v3 situation on the last line. Although this increased the pressure on Galatasaray and led to more turnovers in their build-up, it also raised the risk against long balls due to isolated 1v1s. Time and again, Galatasaray managed to exploit this by sending strong dribblers like Sané into such spacious 1v1 situations. Even so, the tighter marking distances resulted in a much more balanced game with more frequent ball recoveries.

    In the 30th minute, Frankfurt used a longer stoppage to make more significant pressing adjustments. Winger Knauff no longer pressed Galatasaray’s right centre-back but instead oriented himself toward full-back Sallai. This allowed Brown to stay on Sané, and Theate no longer had to make long runs out wide to cover him. At the same time, it was no longer problematic if all four defenders were tied up, as they no longer needed to jump out of the back line. The free centre-back was now primarily pressed by Uzun, who used his cover shadow to block passing lanes into pivot Torreira. Galatasaray’s build-up on the right side could then be pressed man-to-man through ball-oriented shifting. To this end, Chaibi stepped onto Uzun’s original opponent, Torreira, and the far-side Doan also moved into the ball-near center.

    Frankfurt’s pressing adjustments: With no need to shift across the last line anymore, Frankfurt gains situationally much better access with less risk. These changes spark the turnaround in the match.

    According to recent reports, the pressing adjustments led to significantly better situational access and, at the same time, to much stronger defensive security. Frankfurt were able to use the resulting ball recoveries to establish longer possession phases, which gave them a more dominant style of play. One such spell of possession resulted in the 2-1 lead shortly before halftime. Immediately afterwards, a ball recovery from the adjusted attacking press led to a free kick, which in turn produced the 3-1 at the break.

    In the opening 30 minutes, Galatasaray were able to cause Frankfurt problems, thanks in part to a very elusive build-up play that challenged Frankfurt’s typical pressing approach with its reliance on handover moments. Frankfurt’s adjustments, however, proved perfectly suited to applying pressure more easily while also improving defensive cover. The short interruption of play came at just the right time for Toppmöller and his coaching staff to implement the necessary measures. As a result, the pressing changes were decisive for Frankfurt’s eventual 5-1 victory and a successful start to their Champions League campaign.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy.
    • Nacua is set to miss three high-stakes matchups against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and 49ers before he is eligible to return on December 20, in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.
    • In a recent development, the NFL did not publicly disclose the nature of Nacua's personal conduct policy violation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Nacua's suspension takes effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14, after the Rams' key divisional game against the San Francisco 49ers.

    Nacua is set to miss three high-stakes matchups against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and 49ers before he is eligible to return on December 20, in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.

    In a recent development, the NFL did not publicly disclose the nature of Nacua's personal conduct policy violation. It can be inferred, however, that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.

    In a recent development, the woman filed a temporary restraining order against Nacua in March. The lawsuit also mentioned allegations of gender violence and assault and battery. Nacua's attorney denied the allegations and remarked this is a "blackmail" attempt from the alleged victim on December 31, 2025.

    According to ESPN, the NFL said it communicated to Nacua that "any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league.".

    Recent findings suggest that as unfortunate as the suspension is for Nacua, the timing is convenient. The Rams placed him on injured reserve on November 12 due to his PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, so he was already set to miss at least four games during his recovery. Players may serve suspensions while on injured reserve, so he will complete the three-game ban during the remainder of his minimum IR stint. While suspended, Nacua will not be allowed in the team facilities, meaning he will not be allowed to rehab his injury with the team until the suspension is over.

    Previous instances of players serving suspensions while on injured reserve include Daniel Ekuale (2025), Sam Williams (2024), Mike Woods (2023), and David Parry (2018).

    Nacua already missed two games this season due to a hip injury, and the Rams went 1-1 in his absence in Weeks 2 and 3 against the Upcoming York Giants and Denver Broncos. Davante Adams stepped up in a massive way as the team's No. 1 receiver and racked up 332 yards in those contests. Adams remains in the midst of his recovery from a hamstring injury but could return for the Rams' battle with the Packers, which would put him back at the top of the receiving pecking order.

    When he is on the field, Nacua remains a top-flight wide receiver. He averages 102.1 yards per game this year, which is high enough to make him the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards per game at 96.2 over his career.

    Nacua has been a massive piece of the Rams' offensive game proposal and saw at least seven targets in each of his first seven games of the year. He amassed a whopping 24 targets in Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills, which were the most by any player in a single game since 2009.

    #50153. How Aidan Hutchinson injury could grant Lions a salary cap credit in 2027

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (659 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    How Aidan Hutchinson injury could grant Lions a salary cap credit in 2027

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the loss of star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack in Week 10, is a brutal blow to the Detroit Lions in their hunt for the NFC North title and beyond.
    • In the massive four-year, $180 million contract extension Hutchinson signed in 2025, there is a clause that permits the Lions to purchase insurance policies against his salary, according to the Detroit Free Press.
    • The contract reportedly states that the Lions are entitled to purchase insurance policies naming them as beneficiaries for up to $60 million in lost salary if Hutchinson cannot play due to injury.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the loss of star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack in Week 10, is a brutal blow to the Detroit Lions in their hunt for the NFC North title and beyond. There is a silver lining to the injury, though. Clauses in Hutchinson's contract and the NFL's collective bargaining agreement with the NFL Players Association open the door for the Lions to potentially gain financial flexibility as a result of his looming absence.

    In the massive four-year, $180 million contract extension Hutchinson signed in 2025, there is a clause that permits the Lions to purchase insurance policies against his salary, according to the Detroit Free Press.

    The contract reportedly states that the Lions are entitled to purchase insurance policies naming them as beneficiaries for up to $60 million in lost salary if Hutchinson cannot play due to injury. For this season specifically, the Lions may insure up to $45 million. That sum includes $15 million of his signing bonus, the full $28.4 million option bonus and his $1.2 million base salary.

    It is unknown whether the Lions purchased those policies and, if so, whether they maximized them.

    Not only would the Lions earn a prorated amount of Hutchinson's salary as an insurance payment, but the CBA would also allow them to receive salary cap credits in future years to offset the difference between Hutchinson's pay and the insurance proceeds.

    In a recent development, hutchinson's salary and bonuses still count toward the 2026 salary cap, but the Lions could free up millions of dollars in space for 2027 if they purchased sizable insurance policies. According to Over The Cap, Detroit owns the fourth-most cap space this year at $32.9 million and ninth most in 2027 at $62.1 million. Multiple key players, including tight end Sam LaPorta and safety Brian Branch, will reach free agency at the end of this season, so maximizing 2027 cap space would help the Lions re-sign them to larger contracts.

    It has been revealed that salary insurance is expensive, and the Lions do not purchase policies for all players. They reportedly did not insure quarterback Jared Goff's contract when he inked an extension in 2024, nor did they insure linebacker Jack Campbell offseason deal. Campbell suffered a severe neck injury in Week 8, and it is unclear when -- or even if -- he will return to the football field.

    It has been revealed that language about salary cap credits for insurance payments first appeared in the CBA in 2006. It took a few years for teams to take advantage of the clause. A CBS Sports report in 2024 found that the New York Giants included an insurance clause in the addendum to Eli Manning's historic 2009 contract extension that made him the highest-paid player in the NFL. And the earliest known instance of a team qualifying for the cap credit came in 2013 when the Green Bay Packers insured $20 million of Aaron Rodgers' $35 million signing bonus.

    The Lions have a history of insuring their largest contracts. They did so in 2017, when they took out a policy on Matthew Stafford's five-year, $135 million extension. Interestingly, they did not do the same when they re-signed Goff. And as of Oct. 2024, Goff's contract was the only one out of the 13 quarterbacks who earned an average of $45 million per year or more that was not insured.

    Salary cap credits tied to these insurance policies tend to be more modest than one might think. The policies typically require players to miss a certain number of games before payouts begin. Sometimes there is a deductible associated with the policy. This reduces the total payout and, in turn, the amount of cap relief teams receive from the NFL.

    Here are a few examples of cap credits teams received as part of their insurance policies:.

    Torn ACL, strained hamstring (15 games).
